patch.value:
## Source

GitHub #1140: https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1140

## Scope

Own one SDK-level grammar and mutation contract for file and test entries across create, update, dedicated CLI commands, MCP, and public SDK adapters. A comma-bearing value without an explicit leading key must never silently become an unusable path or command. Literal commas remain expressible through explicit keyed or JSON input.

## Context integrity

Project management equals context management: linked artifacts are executable context, so a successful mutation receipt must not certify a path that cannot resolve or a test command that cannot run solely because an advertised tuple form was parsed as plaintext.
GH-1140: reject ambiguous bare comma tuples for linked file and test mutations

GitHub issue #1140 proves that update/create --file and linked-test add paths accept a comma-bearing bare value with no structured key before the first comma, persist the entire tuple as path or command, and return success. The result is a linked file that cannot resolve or a linked test that cannot execute, while TOON rendering can make the corruption look like a valid row.

A shared public SDK parser rejects ambiguous comma-bearing bare file and test entries before mutation with a stable typed refusal and token-efficient keyed/JSON recovery; explicit path= and command= forms preserve literal commas losslessly; create, update, files, test, CLI, SDK, MCP, contracts, completions, and help expose one consistent grammar; health and validation identify legacy corrupted rows without rewriting history; focused unit/integration/packed npm+npx+bun+bunx/temp-workspace acceptance plus literal 100/100/100/100 coverage, docstrings, static, and security gates pass
All-status duplicate search remains distinct from the closed structured-key, unknown-key, docs-pair, and delimiter-safe removal fixes; the exact accepted grammar is specified before implementation.
Make every linked file and test mutation lossless, executable, and self-describing across SDK and CLI entry points.
Agents can trust a successful linked-artifact write without reopening JSON to detect silent tuple corruption.
Prevents durable false context and permanently unrunnable verification evidence.
Issue #1140 reports 38 corrupted items across 16 repositories on versions through 2026.8.28, demonstrating a recurring fleet-wide agent UX failure.

Run pm update <id> --file ".github/workflows/release.yml,project,the publish step" or pm test <id> --add "node scripts/verify.ts,project,120"; read the item as JSON and observe the entire tuple stored in path or command.
Ambiguous comma tuples refuse before mutation with a stable code and keyed/JSON recovery; explicit keyed inputs preserve legitimate commas.
The mutation exits successfully and stores the complete comma-joined tuple in the first field, creating an unresolved path or unrunnable command.
SDK linked-artifact input grammar and CLI adapters
Agents receive successful writes for unusable context and verification evidence; observed across 38 items in 16 repositories.

value.author: harness:codex
value.text: Design boundary: do not reject all commas. The ambiguity predicate is a comma-bearing plaintext candidate without an explicit recognized key before the first delimiter. Keyed path=/command= and JSON inputs must preserve literal commas byte-for-byte. The shared public SDK owns parsing/refusal; CLI and MCP remain adapters.

value.author: harness:codex
value.text: A permissive plaintext fallback becomes silent data corruption when the same option advertises structured comma syntax. Input grammar must make ambiguous encodings unrepresentable or refuse them before durable context is written.
